newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 6.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Inflation will be no lower than 5.2 percent by end-1997, following figures yesterday showing May inflation to be standing at 5.4 percent despite changes to the consumer price index and reduced heating petrol.
--The lack of liquidity plaguing the interbank market over the past few days led to a loss of gains for bonds in the secondary market as well as an increase in long-term interbank interest rates.
--There is disagreement over the price OTE - Greece' telecoms organisation - should set for its new shares. Discussion is focused on 6,500 drachmas and higher.

--The fall in interest rates is slowing to a walk, following the announcement of a 5.4 percent rate for May - that served to dampen the government's optimism - and experts say its downward course will only pick up with "bold structural measures".

--Greece's domestic borrowing programme for the rest of the year was revealed yesterday by Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis, satisfying a standing demand of the market for advance notice of new issues.
--Commercial Bank is against the idea of selling Ionian and in favour of close cooperation if not merger. The final results of a study conducted by Monitor will be released by the end of the year.
--Profits and deposits are up by 20 percent at Commercial bank in first quarter 1997 fostering hopes that profits for the bank this year will be significantly up on 1996.
--Olympic Airways yesterday withdrew its proposal for an 11 percent increase in tickets, following notice from the government that it would not approve such an anti-inflationary move.
